steps.detail: PHP lists upstream releases 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35 for CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619. steps.title: PHP susceptibility advisory - published 2026-10-21
steps.detail: PHP documents an unauthenticated pre-application mod_php demonstration and discusses other SAPIs with susceptibility qualifications. Broad web-serving risk attribution is not proof of equal demonstrated exploitability for every SAPI, configuration, version or patched installation.

steps.title: PHP request-state advisory - published 2026-10-21
steps.detail: The request-state advisory separates concrete demonstrations from candidate cases and configuration-dependent, same-worker request-state paths. Compare the cited SAPI and request prerequisites; this hub has not established them for any deployment.

steps.title: CISA conditional guidance - alert revised 2026-10-23
steps.detail: CISA advises temporary offline status when organizations cannot update immediately or continue using unsupported PHP 8.1 or earlier, until patched or updated. This is attributed guidance under those conditions, not a finding that every numerically older build is unpatched or unpatchable. The retained page does not establish its initial publication time.

steps.title: Separate PHP follow-up - notice published 2026-10-23
steps.detail: The initial-pair release list does not establish a fix for the later CVE-2026-115560. PHP described a next-regular-release plan and session.upload_progress.enabled=0 as an interim setting for an unusual path: php_binary or php_serialize switched to php through ini_set() before session_start(), with upload progress still enabled. That conditional measure is not complete mitigation of the initial pair. These sources do not establish a shipped third fix or historical CVE-registry absence.

cve_briefs.title: Security Advisory 0199

solutions.text: The recommended resolution is to upgrade to a fixed VCO release at your earliest convenience. These vulnerabilities have been fixed in the following releases: - VCO 5.2.3.18 and later in the 5.2 train - VCO 6.1.3.10 and later in the 6.1 train - VCO 6.4.2.12 and later in the 6.4 train

workarounds.text: Until the fixed software is deployed, operators should apply defense-in-depth controls appropriate for their environment: - Restrict access to the VCO web interface to trusted administrative networks. - Monitor the VCO for accesses from known malicious source IPs. - Monitor for unexpected outbound network activity from the VCO host. - Consider blocking outbound ports not needed for normal activities. - Monitor for backdoor daemons and webshells. - Review recent administrator activity for unexpected changes.

limitations: The selection is saved source-declared publications/catalog rows and metadata CVE mentions, not incidents, victims, confirmed exposure or all vulnerabilities.
Date-only rows use a declared UTC-calendar convention with unknown publisher timezone. They are not proven elapsed-hour publication or event instants.
The input was generated after the nominal cutoff and captured later. This is retrospective source/CNA context; zero positive generation tail does not mean complete coverage.
Failed, partial and last-good source observations can leave gaps. A successful status is not exhaustive publisher intake. Raw intake and selection details are not projected.
A CVE missing from a row, including an advisory row, is not proof that the source discusses no CVEs. No identifiers or exploitation claims are inferred from headlines.

All main CVE contexts are retained. Failed/UNKNOWN CNA states, absent CVSS, null workaround text and missing weaknesses remain explicit unknowns. A reference or guidance classification is not a usable workaround.
CNA affected ranges, unaffected products, vendor solution statements, package backports, SAPI/request conditions and CVSS versions remain distinct. No device or patch verification occurred.
CWE/CAPEC mappings classify supplied context; they do not establish an observed attack, actor responsibility, environment applicability or a transitive attribution.
Private editorial titles are not copied. Entries use neutral labels; selected prose is a reviewed paraphrase of accepted metadata/context, not a new publisher-body qualification.
This revision pass performed no new article requests, qualified source checks or comparisons. Unknown/held/not-selected is not updated or unchanged.
CISA catalog addition and due dates are catalog/federal data, not first exploitation times or deadlines assigned to this report’s readers.
Overlapping periods and CVE memberships must not be summed. CNA retrieval/update and publisher evidence clocks remain separate, nullable source fields. None establishes an as-of-cutoff snapshot.
